prompt: Give me a sequence diagram of a customer paying for a salon booking with UPI: the booking page, our backend, Razorpay, the customer's UPI app, and the payment webhook that confirms the booking. Show what happens if the webhook arrives twice.

messages.content: Give me a sequence diagram of a customer paying for a salon booking with UPI: the booking page, our backend, Razorpay, the customer's UPI app, and the payment webhook that confirms the booking. Show what happens if the webhook arrives twice.

content.text: I'll start by looking at what's in the project directory.

input.content:
# Salon booking paid with UPI: sequence diagram Covers the happy path and a duplicate `payment.captured` webhook. Mermaid renders it on GitHub, in VS Code (with a Mermaid extension) and at mermaid.live. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor C as Customer participant P as Booking page participant B as Our backend participant R as Razorpay participant U as UPI app rect rgb(240, 245, 255) Note over C,R: 1. Create booking and order C->>P: Pick service and slot, tap Pay P->>B: POST /bookings (service, slot) B->>B: Save booking as PENDING_PAYMENT and hold slot for 10 min B->>R: Create Order (amount, receipt = booking_id) R-->>B: order_id B-->>P: order_id, key_id end rect rgb(245, 255, 245) Note over C,U: 2. Customer pays P->>R: Open Checkout, customer chooses UPI R->>U: UPI intent or collect request U->>C: Show amount, ask for UPI PIN C->>U: Enter UPI PIN U-->>R: Payment authorised (via bank and NPCI) R-->>P: Checkout success (payment_id, order_id, signature) P->>B: Poll GET /bookings/:id B-->>P: PENDING_PAYMENT (not confirmed yet) Note right of P: The browser callback is NOT trusted to confirm.
Only the webhook confirms the booking. end rect rgb(255, 250, 235) Note over B,R: 3. Webhook confirms booking (first delivery) R->>B: POST /webhooks/razorpay payment.captured (X-Razorpay-Event-Id: evt_1) B->>B: Verify HMAC signature on raw body B->>B: In one DB transaction:
INSERT evt_1 into processed_events (unique key)
UPDATE booking SET CONFIRMED WHERE status = PENDING_PAYMENT B-->>R: 200 OK B--)C: Send confirmation (SMS / WhatsApp) P->>B: Poll GET /bookings/:id B-->>P: CONFIRMED P-->>C: Show booking confirmed end rect rgb(255, 240, 240) Note over B,R: 4. Duplicate webhook (same event delivered again) Note over R,B: Typical cause: our 200 was slow or lost, so Razorpay retries R->>B: POST /webhooks/razorpay payment.captured (X-Razorpay-Event-Id: evt_1) B->>B: Verify HMAC signature on raw body (valid) B->>B: INSERT evt_1 into processed_events alt evt_1 already exists (unique violation) B->>B: Skip. No status change, no second confirmation message B-->>R: 200 OK (so Razorpay stops retrying) else Unexpected failure (DB down) B-->>R: 500 Note over R,B: Razorpay retries later and the handler runs again safely end end ``` ## Why the duplicate is harmless - **Dedupe key:** the `X-Razorpay-Event-Id` header is stored in `processed_events` with a unique constraint. The database enforces "once only", even if two copies arrive at the same moment on different servers. - **Same transaction as the state change:** the dedupe row and the booking update commit or roll back together. A crash cannot leave the event marked processed with the booking unconfirmed. - **Guarded update:** `WHERE status = PENDING_PAYMENT` makes the booking update idempotent even if the dedupe table is bypassed. - **Always return 200 for a known duplicate:** a 4xx or 5xx would make Razorpay keep retrying. - **Side effects run once:** the confirmation message is sent only when the transaction actually changed the booking, not on a duplicate. ## Assumptions to check against your system - The slot hold is 10 minutes. Use your real value. If the webhook arrives after the hold expires, you need a refund or re-book path. That path is not shown here. - The page polls for status. You could use a websocket or server-sent events instead. - Razorpay talks to the UPI app through the bank and NPCI. This is collapsed into one arrow. - The confirmation message is sent inline after the commit. A queue or outbox would be more robust.

content.text:
I wrote the sequence diagram as Mermaid to `upi-booking-payment.md` in the project folder. I haven't rendered it, so open it in GitHub, VS Code with a Mermaid extension, or mermaid.live to check it.

The diagram has the five participants you listed, plus the customer, and four stages:

1. **Create booking and order.** The page calls our backend, which saves the booking as `PENDING_PAYMENT` and holds the slot. It then creates a Razorpay order and returns the `order_id` to the page.
2. **Customer pays.** Checkout opens with UPI selected, and Razorpay sends an intent or collect request to the UPI app. The customer enters their PIN and Razorpay reports success back to the page. The page only polls our backend and still sees `PENDING_PAYMENT`, because the browser callback isn't trusted to confirm anything.
3. **First webhook.** Razorpay sends `payment.captured`. The backend verifies the signature, then in one transaction records the event ID and moves the booking to `CONFIRMED`. It returns 200 and sends the confirmation message, and the page's next poll shows the booking as confirmed.
4. **Duplicate webhook.** The same event arrives again, for example because our 200 was lost. The signature is valid, but inserting the event ID hits the unique constraint. The backend changes nothing, sends no second message and still returns 200 so Razorpay stops retrying. A separate branch shows a 500 from a real failure, which makes Razorpay retry and rerun the handler safely.

Below the diagram I added a short list of why the duplicate is harmless. It covers the unique event ID, the single transaction, the guarded update and sending the message once.

These parts are my assumptions, so check them against your system:
- **Slot hold:** I used a 10-minute hold. If the webhook arrives after the hold expires, you'd need a refund or re-book path, and I didn't draw one.
- **Status updates:** The page polls for status. You may use websockets or server-sent events instead.
- **UPI path:** The bank and NPCI hop is collapsed into one arrow.
- **Confirmation message:** It is sent inline after the commit. A queue or outbox would be more robust.
